additional_comparison_scope: Report against the separately completed expert-feedback family as well. It changes no fitted loss, mixture member, source inventory or primary within-family panel count.
architecture: Exactly build_member_network(input_dim,hidden_size=64,members=1): two 64-unit ReLU layers and three logits. Reinitialize with the same seed for every variant. No dropout, learned temperature, additional embedding or ensemble expansion.
assessment: Complete all three dates before score reveal. Compare every loss with its exact matched log control, matched fixed blends and the strongest retained complete procedure; report both assets, all dates and natural log loss. These exposed dates cannot satisfy the independent substantial-gain gate. Any promising candidate must transfer across broader dates before promotion.
checkpoint_selection: Maximize previous-noon mean balanced accuracy using original historical priors, then minimize mean natural log loss, then retain the earlier epoch. Identical to fit_confirm_neural. Save every epoch record and exact native checkpoint.
fixed_blends: Average each of the eight new sources 50/50 with its representation-matched original HGB and with deep500_hgb, sixteen blends. Retain the entire completed ordered/Langevin family without changing forecasts. No weight search.
gradient_scale: All losses have exactly the log-loss logit gradient (1/K-one_hot(y)) at uniform q. Pseudospherical gradient is K^alpha*s_y^alpha*(s-one_hot(y)); Brier uses K/2. This fixes one local scale, not the full optimization trajectory, curvature everywhere, effective learning rate everywhere or regularization equivalence.
historical_input_verification: Reconstruct the original normalized historical and validation pools from completed learned-memory artifacts. Require exact source labels, clocks and priors, actual label releases before each partition, and full original neural query-probability parity. All six log controls must reproduce every original state parameter and full query probability exactly.
hypothesis: Test whether bounded strictly proper scoring rules improve finite-sample class discrimination under the same neural architecture and historical information. These rules alter the treatment of hard examples without changing the ideal class-balanced probability target. Boundedness and population propriety do not imply finite-sample calibration, robustness to arbitrary corruption, convex optimization, or a market gain.
log_control: Train all six log-loss controls and require exact state-dictionary and complete forecast parity with the saved original observations_neural/combined_neural models. Failure halts the family before assessment reveal; preserve failures and do not silently weaken parity.

losses.log: Exactly the existing unreduced torch cross_entropy(u,y).
losses.spherical2: For beta=2, alpha=(beta-1)/beta, s=softmax(beta*u), A=K^alpha/(beta-1), L=A*(1-s_y^alpha). Evaluate as -A*expm1(alpha*log_softmax(beta*u)_y).
losses.spherical4: The same pseudospherical proper loss with beta=4. Beta is finite and fixed; no beta-to-infinity or hard 0-1-loss limit is used.

mathematical_verification: Compare stable logit losses against independent probability/norm formulas; analytic gradients against autograd and finite differences; uniform-gradient matching; strict population optima and weighted posterior inversion; permutation and common-logit-shift invariance; extreme finite logits; and tiny-data log-control reproduction against fit_confirm_neural.
partition: Use every original historical d-5 through d-2 stride-four row. Only the previous noon selects an epoch. Preserve all 7070 original noon assessment rows per asset/date. Recheck actual label release clocks, original row/label/time identity and original priors. No assessment label or same-day label enters fitting or checkpoint selection.
population_propriety: For beta>1, s_y^alpha=q_y^(beta-1)/||q||_beta^(beta-1). Holder inequality makes the expected score uniquely maximal at q=eta on the probability simplex. The Brier excess risk is (K/2)*||q-eta||_2^2. Thus all four losses elicit the same ideal balanced posterior. This says nothing about fitted finite-network accuracy or calibration.
preflight: Freeze full-row-count synthetic timing and resource checks separately after mathematical tests. Check every loss at both original input dimensions, native checkpoint recovery, causal prefix/row independence and finite gradients. Freeze limits and source hashes before running; preserve any failure. No paid compute.
preprocessing: Reuse the exact frozen original quantile-normal transform, active columns, feature order and -1/+1 asset indicator. Verify exact normalized historical and validation matrices against completed records. No new features, feature selection, sample selection or query normalization.

primary_sources.scope: Gneiting and Raftery, JASA 2007: strictly proper quadratic, spherical and pseudospherical scores. The registered finite-K formulas and gradient normalization are independently derived; the source does not claim a gain on this market target.
Williamson, Vernet and Reid, JMLR 2016: composite multiclass losses and the distinction between properness, links and other optimization properties.

Zhang and Sabuncu, NeurIPS 2018: generalized cross entropy motivates a different influence of hard examples. We use a proper probability parameterization and make no claim that stochastic market labels are corrupted labels.

probability_target: The network emits logits u and q=softmax(u), interpreted as the class-balanced posterior. Recover natural p proportional to q*pi[asset] with the exact original historical priors. There is no unregistered post-fit temperature, posterior power transform or target relabeling.
raw_gce_distinction: Raw generalized cross entropy (1-s_y^alpha)/alpha has population optimizer s proportional to eta^(1/(1-alpha)); interpreting s directly as eta is incorrect. The registered natural logit parameterization q with s=softmax(beta*u) is the known pseudospherical scoring rule. It needs no inverse-link estimation or calibration fit.
runtime: Use the existing pinned two-thread CPU Torch runtime. Mathematical unit fits may run while another family is active, but no substantial synthetic or market fit runs concurrently with the ordered/Langevin study.
sample_weights: Original float32 balanced_asset_weights: N/(6*n[asset,class]) on natural-order shuffled query minibatches. Keep every original historical row and the same numpy permutation stream across all loss variants.
